title: Grade 6 Science — Mon, May 25
description: Components of Food — Day 1 of 5: Types of nutrients
subject: science

questions.question: The substances in food that provide energy and materials for body processes are called:
questions.explanation: Nutrients are the chemical substances in food that the body uses for energy, growth, and repair.

questions.question: Which nutrient gives the most energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Fats give 9 calories per gram — more than twice the energy from carbohydrates or proteins (4 cal/g each).

questions.question: Carbohydrates are our body's main source of:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates (starch and sugar) are broken down to glucose, which is the main fuel for body cells.

questions.question: Proteins are mainly needed for:
options: Growth and repair of body cells
questions.explanation: Proteins are the building blocks of cells. They're needed for growth, repair of damaged tissues, and making enzymes.

questions.question: Which food is a good source of carbohydrates?
questions.explanation: Rice, wheat, bread, and potatoes are rich in carbohydrates (starch).

questions.question: Which food is a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: Dal, eggs, fish, meat, and milk are rich in proteins.

questions.question: Which of these is a fat?
questions.explanation: Butter, oils, ghee, and nuts are sources of fats.

questions.question: Vitamins and minerals are called 'protective foods' because:
options: They protect the body from diseases and help body functions
questions.explanation: Vitamins and minerals don't give energy but are essential for regulating body processes and protecting against diseases.

questions.question: Which nutrient is needed for strong bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium (found in milk, dairy, green leafy vegetables) is essential for building strong bones and teeth.

questions.question: Dietary fibre (roughage) mainly helps in:
questions.explanation: Roughage (fibre from fruits, vegetables, whole grains) helps in smooth movement of food through the digestive system.

questions.question: Water is needed by the body for:
options: Many vital functions including digestion, transport, and temperature regulation
questions.explanation: Water makes up 60-70% of our body. It is needed for digestion, transportation of nutrients, removal of waste, and regulating body temperature.

questions.question: Which of these provides both protein and fat?
questions.explanation: Eggs contain proteins (in egg white) and fats (in egg yolk) — a very nutritious food.

questions.question: Iron is an important mineral needed for:
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin — the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body.

questions.question: A meal of dal-rice-sabzi-curd is considered balanced because:
options: It contains carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, and minerals
questions.explanation: Dal-rice-sabzi-curd provides carbohydrates (rice), protein (dal, curd), vitamins (sabzi), making it a well-balanced meal.

questions.question: Which is an example of a complete diet?
options: A variety of foods covering all nutrient groups
questions.explanation: A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre — in the right proportions.
